plan: To prioritize capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
These holdings are in downtrends and carry amplified risk.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name limit.
This strategy aims for a lower-drawdown portfolio with a significant cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces portfolio risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside potential.

plan: To balance risk and growth, trim all leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
These holdings are in downtrends and carry amplified risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name limit.

This plan aims for risk-first growth with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential, with a focus on managing downside risk.

plan: To pursue aggressive growth, trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name limit.
Add SPXS at 6%, NVDD at 6%, and AAPU at 6% as high-scoring scanner long setups.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It concentrates in high-scoring scanner setups and utilizes leverage, which amplifies both upside and drawdown. Be aware of significant potential for rapid losses due to leverage decay and market swings; strict stop discipline is critical.

plan: To prioritize income, sell all leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
These holdings are not aligned with an income strategy.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name limit.
Add QQQI to 30% to increase exposure to income-generating assets.
This plan focuses on steady distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, aiming to park cash for yield. It prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown by rotating into income ETFs and cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs; this is not a savings account.
